landing.faq.stack.question: What's the tech stack?
landing.faq.stack.answer: Next.js 16 with the App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM, and better-auth. Every piece of business logic is inlined — no external packages for payment, email, storage, or AI.
landing.faq.payment.question: Which payment providers are supported?
landing.faq.payment.answer: Stripe, PayPal, Creem, Alipay, and WeChat Pay out of the box. The PaymentManager abstraction makes it straightforward to add more providers by implementing a single interface.
landing.faq.database.question: Which databases can I use?
landing.faq.database.answer: Drizzle ORM handles PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Turso, and Cloudflare D1. Switch providers by editing DATABASE_PROVIDER in your .env — the schema templates and drizzle config adapt automatically.
landing.faq.customize.question: How customizable is the landing page?
landing.faq.customize.answer: The src/blocks/ directory ships with demo sections — they're designed to be rewritten per project. The durable primitives live in src/components/, so your rebrand touches blocks and translations, not the chassis.
landing.faq.license.question: Can I use this for commercial projects?
landing.faq.license.answer: Yes. ShipAny Next is built for shipping production SaaS products. You own the code after cloning — no per-seat fees, no runtime dependencies on our infrastructure.

home.meta_title: Remove Matcha Filter Online – Free Photo & Video Tool
home.meta_description: Use this free Matcha Filter remover to reduce the Matcha Filter look in photos and videos. Adjust color, grain and detail locally—no upload or sign-up.
home.h1: Free Matcha Filter Remover for Photos and Videos
home.subhead: Remove the Matcha Filter look by reducing the green cast, added grain and flattened contrast. Preview and export for free—without an upload, account or credits.
home.tool_heading: Start with a photo or a video
home.expect_title: What this matcha filter remover actually does
home.expect_body: A matcha filter is a colour grade: it tints the midtones green, flattens contrast, softens fine texture and often lays grain on top. This tool works the same way in reverse. It measures the colour balance of your own frame, eases the tint back toward neutral, re-stretches the levels, and gives you separate control over grain and micro-detail.
home.expect_honest_body: It cannot recover the original pixels. Once a filter has clipped a highlight or discarded texture, that information is gone from the file you were given — no tool can read it back. What you get is a more natural-looking result, not a reconstruction of the untouched shot.
home.how_title: How to use the Matcha Filter remover
home.how_1_body: Choose an image or clip for the Matcha Filter remover by dragging it in or browsing your files. The browser creates a temporary object URL for local decoding; the tool makes no upload request.
home.how_2_body: Colour, noise and detail start at a moderate default preset. Move one at a time and watch the adjusted panel update live.
home.how_3_body: The original sits beside the result the whole time. When it looks right, export a PNG or a recorded video to your downloads.
home.paths_title: Choose the right Matcha Filter remover
home.paths_photo_body: Use the Matcha Filter remover for one photo or screenshot at a time, at up to 4096px on the long edge, with PNG export.
home.paths_video_body: Use the Matcha Filter remover for a video clip that renders frame by frame, keeps supported audio and records to a downloadable file.
home.privacy_title: Why this Matcha Filter remover stays private
home.privacy_body: The Matcha Filter remover has no upload step because there is no server-side processing. Your file is read by the browser, rendered on a canvas by your own GPU, and exported straight back to your downloads folder. Close the tab and nothing remains.
home.sources_intro: This page separates facts about the shipped tool from interpretation. The limits below come from the current implementation, while the linked primary specifications explain the browser APIs used for local files, WebGL rendering and video recording.
home.sources_byline: Published by Matcha Filter Remover Team · Maintained by Jared
home.sources_file_api: W3C File API — browser object URLs
home.sources_github: Official GitHub repository — implementation and QA
home.faq_q1: Can the original unfiltered image be fully recovered?
home.faq_a1: No. The filter discarded and overwrote information before you received the file, and no tool can read back what is not there. This tool reduces the filter look — the green cast, the flattened contrast, the grain — so the result looks more natural. Treat it as a better-looking edit, not a recovered original.
home.faq_q2: Are my photos or videos uploaded?
home.faq_a2: No. There is no upload step and no server-side processing. Your browser decodes the file, your GPU renders the adjusted version, and the export is written straight to your downloads. We never receive your media, so there is nothing for us to store or inspect.
home.faq_q3: Why does this Matcha Filter remover give different results by file?
home.faq_a3: The correction is measured from your own frame, and it can only work with what survived. A lightly filtered photo has most of its colour relationships intact and cleans up well. A heavily graded one, with clipped highlights and crushed shadows, improves but cannot be brought back to neutral convincingly.
home.faq_q4: Do I need to install a Matcha Filter Remover app?
home.faq_a4: No. The tool works online in a current Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox browser, while your media is processed locally on your device. There is no app, APK, extension, account or upload step. Video export additionally needs canvas recording, which is most reliable in recent Chrome, Edge and Firefox.
home.faq_q5: Why does the Matcha Filter remover take longer to export video?
home.faq_a5: Export records the canvas while the clip plays, in real time — a 30-second clip takes about 30 seconds. There is no server farm to hand the work to, which is the same reason your video never leaves your device.
photo.meta_title: Remove Matcha Filter from Photo Online – Free Tool
photo.meta_description: Remove the Matcha filter look from a photo for free. Correct color, grain and detail locally, compare the result and download a PNG.
photo.h1: Remove Matcha Filter from a Photo
photo.subhead: Correct the green cast, added grain and softened detail in one image. Processing stays on your device and the result exports as a lossless PNG.
photo.body_title: How this Matcha Filter remover works on a photo
photo.body_1: Photos give you the most room to work. The whole frame is measured once when you load it, so the colour correction is fitted to your specific image rather than to a generic matcha look, and every slider change re-renders the full-resolution result immediately.
photo.body_2: Start with colour. It carries most of the visible change: the green tint eases out of the midtones and the levels re-stretch to the black and white points found in your frame. Then add noise reduction only as far as the grain needs, and reach for detail last — it exaggerates whatever texture survived, including compression artefacts.
photo.tip_1: Judge the result at full size, not the shrunk preview. Fine texture and denoise smearing both hide at small scale.
photo.tip_2: If skin turns magenta, colour is too high. The correction assumes the average of your frame should be neutral, which overshoots when the subject really is green.
photo.tip_3: Detail above roughly 60 starts to look crunchy on phone photos, which are already sharpened in-camera.
photo.tip_4: PNG export is lossless, so the file will be larger than the JPEG you started from.
video.meta_title: Remove Matcha Filter from Video Online – Free Tool
video.meta_description: Reduce the Matcha Filter look in TikTok and other videos: correct green color, grain and flat contrast frame by frame, then export locally with supported audio.
video.h1: Free Matcha Filter Remover for Video
video.subhead: Remove the Matcha Filter look from a clip frame by frame. Preview beside the source, then export locally with its audio when supported.
video.body_title: How this Matcha Filter remover works on video
video.body_1: Each frame goes through exactly the same single-pass adjustment as a photo — the same shader, the same three controls. The difference is that it runs on every frame while the clip plays, so what you see in the adjusted panel is the finished look, live.
video.body_2: The Matcha Filter remover measures the first frame, keeps that correction stable across the clip, and renders at up to 1920px on the long edge. Stable settings prevent colour or brightness shifts at scene changes while keeping 4K phone footage practical on ordinary hardware.
video.export_1: Export records the canvas in real time while the clip plays start to finish. A 30-second clip takes about 30 seconds, and the tab needs to stay in the foreground — background tabs get throttled and drop frames.
video.export_2: The export keeps the source audio track when the browser can read it. Recording follows live playback, so picture and sound stay aligned. If the audio cannot be read, the export is blocked with an explanation instead of producing a silent file.
video.export_3: Video export needs MediaRecorder with canvas capture. Recent Chrome, Edge and Firefox handle it; Safari's support is newer and less reliable. Adjusting and previewing work everywhere WebGL does.
video.tip_1: Trim before you load. Recording is realtime, so a shorter clip is a shorter wait.
video.tip_2: Re-export HEVC footage as H.264 MP4 first — most browsers outside Safari cannot decode it at all.
video.tip_3: Keep noise reduction lower than you would on a photo. Frame-by-frame denoise can shimmer between frames in a way a still never shows.
site.footer.tagline: Reduce the matcha filter look — in your browser, on your device.

examples.title: Before and after
examples.intro: These comparisons were made with the current tool and our own AI-generated test photos, then given a matcha-style grade. They are demonstrations, not customer results. Move the divider to compare.
examples.honest: Results vary with the source file. A lightly filtered photo cleans up convincingly; a heavily crushed one improves but will not look untouched.
examples.pending: Example comparisons are being produced from our own test media and will appear here. We would rather show nothing than borrow someone else's photos.
examples.ex1_body: The default settings reduce the green cast across skin, a cream blouse and a concrete wall. Look at the face and white fabric first: they reveal an overcorrection faster than a colourful background does.
examples.ex2_body: A social-video style frame tests skin, a blue shirt and mixed window and studio light together. This is a still-image demonstration; videos use the same correction frame by frame in the video tool.
examples.ex3_body: Three people, three clothing colours and warm wood make this a harder balance test. The moderate preset eases the shared green tint without forcing every skin tone or fabric into the same colour.
examples.ex4_body: Blue sky, white walls and terracotta roofs expose colour shifts that a close portrait can hide. Check that the whites look neutral while the blues and warm details stay distinct.
examples.ex5_body: Unbranded packaging, glass, linen and a camera show whether edges and small textures survive the adjustment. The tool reduces the cast; it does not replace labels or invent missing product detail.
examples.ex6_body: White ceramics, red fruit, orange juice, blue fabric and oak give the correction several reference colours at once. A natural result keeps those differences instead of turning the whole table cold.
home.faq_q6: Is this Matcha Filter Remover free?
home.faq_a6: Yes. This free Matcha Filter Remover runs on your hardware, so there is no per-file cost, account or credit requirement.
photo.faq_q1: Which image formats can I use?
photo.faq_a1: PNG, JPEG, WebP and AVIF, up to 25 MB. Those are the types we have tested. Export is always PNG, which is lossless — expect a larger file than the JPEG you started with.
photo.faq_q2: Does it change my original file?
photo.faq_a2: Never. The original is only read, and the adjusted version is a separate download. Your source file is untouched on disk.
photo.faq_q3: Why does the result look worse when I raise Detail?
photo.faq_a3: Detail sharpens whatever texture survived the filter, including compression artefacts. Phone photos are already sharpened in-camera, so values above roughly 60 tend to look crunchy.
video.faq_q1: Which video formats can I use?
video.faq_a1: MP4, MOV and WebM, up to 200 MB, as long as your browser can decode them. HEVC-encoded MOV files generally fail outside Safari — re-export those as H.264 MP4 or WebM first.
video.faq_q2: Does the exported video keep the original sound?
video.faq_a2: When the source clip has an audio track, the export carries it through and stays in sync, because recording follows live playback. A silent source stays silent. If this browser cannot read the audio track at all, the tool stops and says so rather than handing you a silent file — we would rather block the export than quietly drop your sound.
video.faq_q3: Can I close the tab while it exports?
video.faq_a3: No. Recording follows live playback in this tab, so closing it, or in some browsers switching away, interrupts the export. The tool warns you while a recording is running.
video.faq_a4: Clips are rendered up to 1920px on the long edge. That ceiling keeps realtime recording achievable on ordinary hardware; photos are not limited this way.
tool.audio_absent: The source had no audio, so the export is video only.
video.tip_4: Keep the tab in the foreground while exporting. Background tabs can throttle playback, which affects both the recording and its audio.
tool.audio_attached: The original audio track was attached to the recording — play the file to confirm the sound came through.
tool.audio_unavailable: This browser could not read the audio track from your video, so exporting now could silently drop the original sound. We cannot confirm whether your file has audio. Try the latest Chrome, Edge, or Firefox to export with sound.
home.naming_title: How This Matcha Filter Remover Handles Photos and Videos
home.naming_body: “Matcha effect remover” is another phrase people use for this workflow. The tool reduces the visible green cast, added grain and flattened contrast locally, without claiming to reconstruct missing pixels.
photo.intent_line: Use this page to remove the Matcha filter look from a photo—one image at a time, at full resolution, with the original beside the result.
video.intent_line: Use this page to remove the Matcha Filter look from a video clip. The same three controls are applied frame by frame as it plays.
home.faq_q7: Can I remove the Matcha filter from a TikTok video?
home.faq_a7: Yes—save a clip you own or have permission to edit, then open it in the video tool. The color cast, added grain and compressed contrast can be reduced. The tool cannot reveal hidden content or recreate pixels the effect replaced, covered or removed.
home.trend_title: What is the Matcha Filter trend?
home.trend_body_1: The Matcha Filter name is being used for a green, creamy, high-texture look shared across short-form photos and videos. Some versions behave like a strong colour grade; others transform the image more aggressively. That distinction matters because colour, contrast and added grain can often be reduced, while replaced shapes or missing pixels cannot be reversed.
home.trend_body_2: People looking for a Matcha Filter remover usually want one of two things: a more natural colour balance or a clear answer about whether the untouched original can be recovered. This tool handles the first job locally and explains the boundary of the second before you export.
home.naming_body_2: The Matcha Filter remover measures a photo once and can export it at up to 4096px on the long edge. For video, it applies the same correction to every frame and records in real time at up to 1920px. Choose the dedicated page for format-specific tips, compatibility and export details.
home.guide_card_title: How to remove Matcha Filter step by step
home.guide_card_body: Use the Matcha Filter remover controls in the right order, judge the recovery boundary and troubleshoot common photo and video problems.
home.trend_card_body: See what creates the green liquid look, why removal results vary and how correction differs from AI reconstruction.
recovery.title: What this Matcha filter remover can—and cannot—recover
recovery.intro: A finished image only contains the pixels that survived the effect and later compression. Use this boundary as a realistic guide: correction can rebalance visible information, but it cannot retrieve information that is no longer in the file.
recovery.row_1_expectation: Colour correction can move green midtones toward a more neutral balance, although genuinely green objects may also shift.
recovery.row_2_expectation: Moderate smoothing can calm overlaid grain while preserving strong edges. Heavy settings may smear fine detail.
recovery.row_3_expectation: Surviving black and white points can be stretched, but clipped highlights and crushed shadows contain no hidden tonal range.
recovery.row_4_expectation: A deterministic colour-and-detail correction does not guess where altered facial features, objects or edges used to be.
recovery.row_5_expectation: The tool cannot reveal censored, hidden or transformed content. Those original pixels are absent from the file.
photo.body_3: Unlike a generative AI editor, this photo correction workflow does not redraw the subject or send the image to a model. The same input and settings produce the same correction, which makes the result easier to inspect and keeps private media on your device.
photo.workflow_title: A practical correction order for photos
photo.workflow_1_body: Raise Colour until neutral references—skin, paper, walls or grey objects—stop looking green. Back off as soon as skin turns pink or truly green objects start looking blue.
photo.workflow_2_body: Increase Noise only enough to calm the filter texture. Check hair, eyelashes, fabric and text at full size; those areas reveal smoothing damage before the preview does.
photo.workflow_3_body: Use Detail to recover edge clarity after smoothing. It cannot recreate lost texture, and high values also sharpen JPEG blocks, halos and phone-camera processing.
photo.guide_cta: Open the full photo and video guide
photo.faq_q4: Can I remove the Matcha Filter from a TikTok photo or screenshot?
photo.faq_a4: Yes, if you own the image or are allowed to edit it. A screenshot usually carries extra compression, so use less Detail and judge text edges carefully. The tool adjusts visible color and texture; it does not reveal anything that was covered or removed.
photo.faq_title: Matcha Filter Remover for Photos FAQ
video.body_3: The correction remains deterministic: it adjusts visible colour, contrast, grain and edge detail rather than asking an AI model to imagine a new clip. That avoids invented faces or backgrounds and keeps the source video inside the browser tab.
video.faq_title: Matcha Filter Remover for Video FAQ
video.tiktok_title: How to Remove the Matcha Filter from a TikTok Video
video.tiktok_body_1: To remove the Matcha Filter from a TikTok video, start with the highest-quality copy you own or have permission to edit. Social-platform downloads are already compressed, so block edges, banding and sharpened captions become more obvious when Detail is too high. Trim the clip first because export runs for the full duration in real time.
video.tiktok_body_2: This workflow can reduce a green cast, added grain and flattened contrast across the visible frames. It cannot recover a face, background, text or object that a transformation changed or removed. It also does not download content from TikTok or any other platform; you choose a local file yourself.
video.tiktok_summary_title: Working with a saved TikTok clip
video.tiktok_summary_body: Use the highest-quality local copy you own or may edit, keep correction conservative around captions and compression, and open the dedicated TikTok workflow for source and export details. For any other local video, continue with the general workflow on this page.
video.evidence_title: A real browser export, not a photo standing in for video

trend.meta_title: Matcha Filter Trend: What It Is & How to Reduce It
trend.meta_description: Matcha Filter is a green, creamy visual trend—not one official filter. See what “without filter” can mean, what can be reduced, and what cannot be recovered.
trend.h1: What Is the Matcha Filter Trend?
trend.lede: Matcha Filter is a community name for a green, creamy family of visual effects—not one permanent official filter. Here is what an unfiltered result can mean, what visible treatment can be reduced, and why missing source pixels cannot be recovered.
trend.fact_1_value: Photos, screenshots and short video clips
trend.fact_2_value: Green midtones, softer texture, compressed contrast and added grain
trend.fact_3_value: Deterministic WebGL processing in your browser
trend.fact_4_value: Visible colour and texture can be adjusted; replaced pixels cannot be restored
trend.what_body_1: Matcha Filter is a community name for a family of green visual treatments rather than one permanent, official platform setting. The shared cue is a matcha-like palette: yellow-green midtones, creamy highlights, softened local texture and a layer of grain or liquid-looking detail. A photo may simply be colour graded, while a more extreme version may distort or regenerate parts of the scene.
trend.what_body_2: That range explains why examples do not all respond the same way. If the source still contains the original shapes and most of its tonal information, colour and contrast correction can make it look substantially more natural. If an effect rebuilt a face, changed geometry or painted over part of the image, no slider can know what the missing pixels originally contained.
trend.without_title: What does the Matcha trend look like without the filter?
trend.without_body_1: Reducing the green cast, added grain and flattened contrast usually produces a more natural-looking version with clearer neutral colours and more separation between light and dark areas. The result still depends on how strongly the source was processed and compressed.
trend.without_body_2: “Without the filter” should mean a corrected edit, not the untouched original. If the effect replaced geometry, covered content or discarded pixels, only the original source file contains that missing information.
trend.layers_title: Five visual layers behind the Matcha look
trend.layers_intro: You do not need to identify every layer before editing, but separating them helps you choose the right control and stop before the image looks overprocessed.
trend.layer_1_body: Midtones shift toward olive or yellow-green, which is especially obvious in skin, white walls and neutral clothing.
trend.layer_2_body: Highlights and shadows move closer together, producing a creamy, poster-like image with less separation.
trend.layer_3_body: Fine texture is softened so skin, fabric and background detail feel blended or poured rather than sharply photographed.
trend.layer_4_body: Edges around faces, hair and objects may be sharpened or redrawn, creating a graphic outline around smoother interiors.
trend.layer_5_body: Still images may carry visible speckle; videos can add moving texture that changes from frame to frame and is harder to smooth cleanly.
trend.spread_title: Why people search for a Matcha filter remover
trend.spread_body_1: Short-form trends often move faster than their vocabulary. One common search, “Matcha trend filter remover,” combines two intentions: understanding the trend and making an existing file look less processed. Related phrases such as “remove Matcha Filter” and “Matcha Filter remover” describe the same correction goal in a different word order.
trend.spread_body_2: A useful removal page needs to answer both without pretending they are the same problem. This explainer covers the context and recovery boundary; the browser tool handles visible colour, grain and detail. The complete guide shows how to tune those controls for a photo or video.
trend.adult_title: Is the Matcha Filter trend NSFW?
trend.adult_body_1: Some posts use the look inside reveal-style jokes or attach suggestive framing to it, which is why the term may appear beside adult-language discussions. That context is not a technical property of the visual effect and is not required to understand or reduce it.
trend.adult_body_2: This site only adjusts media you choose locally. It does not reveal covered bodies, remove censorship, infer hidden content or support non-consensual editing. If pixels were hidden or replaced, they are not present for the tool to recover.
trend.official_title: Is it an official TikTok or Instagram filter?
trend.official_body_1: The name is used inconsistently across posts, prompts, edits and third-party tools. A specific effect may be recreated by several apps or AI workflows, and platform catalog names can change. Do not assume two files labelled “Matcha Filter” were produced by the same process.
trend.official_body_2: Remove Matcha Filter is independent and is not operated, sponsored or endorsed by TikTok, Instagram or their owners. You provide a local file; the site does not connect to a social account or scrape a platform URL.
trend.remove_title: How to reduce the Matcha Filter look
trend.remove_body_1: Use Colour first to rebalance the green cast, Noise second to calm added texture and Detail last to restore edge clarity. Compare neutral references in the original and adjusted panels, then stop at the lightest correction that solves the visible problem.
trend.faq_title: Questions about the Matcha Filter trend
trend.faq_q1: Can the Matcha Filter be completely reversed?
trend.faq_a1: Only if “reversed” means reducing visible color, contrast and grain. An untouched original cannot be recovered from pixels that were clipped, distorted, covered or replaced.
trend.faq_q2: Does removing the green color restore the original photo?
trend.faq_a2: No. Better color can make the file look more natural, but it does not recreate lost texture, highlights, shadows or geometry. Treat the result as a corrected edit.
trend.faq_q3: Why do some Matcha images need AI reconstruction?
trend.faq_a3: Some examples are generated transformations rather than color grades. Reconstructing them requires a model to imagine new pixels. That can produce a plausible picture, but it is a new interpretation—not a recovered original.
trend.faq_q4: Can this tool process both photos and videos?
trend.faq_a4: Yes. Photos render at up to 4096px on the long edge and export as PNG. Videos apply the same correction frame by frame at up to 1920px and record in real time.
trend.faq_a5: No. The file is decoded, adjusted and exported in your browser. The site never receives the photo or video.
trend.callout_body: Use this tool when the visible subject is still present and you want a less green, less grainy, more natural-looking edit. If the effect replaced the scene, only the original source file can provide the original pixels.
guide.meta_title: How to Remove Matcha Filter from Photos & Videos (Free Guide)
guide.meta_description: Follow the safest order to remove the Matcha Filter look from a photo or video: correct color, reduce grain, restore detail and export locally.
guide.h1: How to Remove Matcha Filter from a Photo or Video
guide.lede: A practical workflow for reducing the green cast, added grain and flattened contrast without uploading your media or asking AI to invent a replacement image.
guide.before_title: Before you begin: choose the best source
guide.before_body_1: Use the original file or the highest-quality copy you are allowed to edit. Every screenshot, social download and messaging-app resend adds compression. Correction can make those artefacts more visible, especially around captions, hair and high-contrast edges.
guide.before_body_2: Check whether the subject and background still have their original shapes. If they do, deterministic correction is a strong first choice. If the scene was transformed into new liquid forms or painted over, expect an improved colour balance—not a recovered original.
guide.note_body: Use the least correction that solves the visible problem. A natural result usually comes from three moderate moves, not one slider pushed to its maximum.
guide.steps_title: Remove the Matcha Filter look in five steps
guide.step_1_body: Open the matching tool and choose a local PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, MP4, MOV or WebM within the stated size limit. The browser creates a temporary local URL; the file is not sent to this site or a third-party processor.
guide.step_2_body: Move Colour gradually while watching skin, whites, grey surfaces and other neutral references. Stop when the green bias eases. If skin turns magenta or foliage becomes blue, the correction has gone too far.
guide.step_3_body: Increase Noise until distracting speckle settles, then inspect fine edges at full size. Hair, fabric, eyelashes and small text reveal smoothing damage early. Videos usually need less smoothing because frame-to-frame changes can shimmer.
guide.step_4_body: Raise Detail only after colour and noise are settled. The control improves edge clarity; it does not regenerate missing texture. High values also sharpen compression blocks and halos, so judge the full-size result rather than the small preview.
guide.step_5_body: Switch your attention between the original and adjusted panels instead of chasing a perfectly neutral histogram. Export the photo as PNG or keep the video tab in the foreground while it records in real time. Play a video export once to confirm picture and sound.
guide.format_title: Photo and video need different expectations
guide.format_1_value: Up to 4096px on the long edge, exported as lossless PNG
guide.format_2_value: Up to 1920px on the long edge, recorded in real time
guide.format_3_value: Attached when the browser can read the source track; export is blocked when sound cannot be verified
guide.format_4_value: Both workflows decode and render inside the current browser tab
guide.problems_title: Common problems and the right fix
guide.problem_1_body: Lower Colour. The frame may contain genuinely green scenery, so an average-neutral correction can overshoot the subject.
guide.problem_2_body: Lower Noise and check at full size. Smoothing cannot distinguish added filter grain from every strand or letter edge.
guide.problem_3_body: Lower Detail. Phone sharpening and social compression are already baked into the file and become exaggerated quickly.
guide.problem_4_title: A video will not open or export
guide.problem_4_body: Convert HEVC footage to H.264 MP4 or WebM and use a recent Chrome, Edge or Firefox. Keep the tab visible until real-time recording finishes.
guide.finish_title: Ready to make the lightest useful correction?
guide.finish_body: Start with the format-specific tool. Your media stays local, the controls update the preview immediately, and you can reset at any time if the edit moves away from a natural result.
guide.schema_tool_media: A photo or video you have permission to edit
guide.photo_cta: Remove Matcha Filter from a photo
guide.video_cta: Remove Matcha Filter from a video
guide.faq_q1: What settings should I start with?
guide.faq_a1: Use the moderate default preset, then tune Colour first, Noise second and Detail last. There is no universal perfect value because every source has a different grade and compression history.
guide.faq_q2: Can I undo a Matcha Filter without the original file?
guide.faq_a2: You can reduce visible treatment in the copy you have. You cannot recover pixels that only exist in the missing original, so the result is a correction rather than a true undo.
guide.faq_q3: Is AI required to remove the Matcha Filter?
guide.faq_a3: Not when the visible subject is intact and the main problems are color, grain and contrast. This tool uses deterministic browser processing. AI reconstruction is a different task that invents plausible replacement pixels.
guide.faq_q4: Why should I correct color before detail?
guide.faq_a4: Color causes most of the Matcha look. Fixing it first lets you judge how much texture work is actually necessary and avoids sharpening grain that you later smooth away.
guide.faq_q5: Does the tool keep my photo or video?
guide.faq_a5: No. It uses a temporary browser URL and your device's GPU. Close the tab and that local working state disappears.

tiktok.meta_title: How to Remove Matcha Filter on TikTok – Free Video Tool
tiktok.meta_description: Use a free local video tool to reduce the Matcha Filter look in a TikTok video. Correct green color, grain and detail, then export with supported audio.
tiktok.h1: How to Remove the Matcha Filter from a TikTok Video
tiktok.subhead: Choose a TikTok video you own or have permission to edit. The tool works locally in your browser—no TikTok URL, account connection or upload to our servers.
tiktok.source_title: Start with the cleanest video you can access
tiktok.source_body_1: The original camera file or an editor export usually preserves more color and edge detail than a social download, screen recording or messaging-app copy. Use that source when you have it. If the TikTok copy is all you have, the tool can still reduce the visible treatment, but it cannot reverse compression that is already baked in.
tiktok.source_body_2: Only edit media you own or are allowed to use. This page does not fetch, scrape or download videos from TikTok, and it is not affiliated with or endorsed by TikTok.
tiktok.steps_title: Remove the Matcha Filter look in five controlled steps
tiktok.step_1_body: Select a supported MP4, MOV or WebM from your device. If a phone recording uses HEVC and will not open, convert a copy to H.264 MP4 first.
tiktok.step_2_body: Adjust Colour first. Watch skin, white clothing and grey surfaces, and stop before natural greens turn blue or skin shifts toward magenta.
tiktok.step_3_body: Raise Noise gradually. Check captions, hair and fabric at full size because social compression and smoothing can make those edges look waxy.
tiktok.step_4_body: Increase Detail only after color and noise look balanced. It can clarify existing edges, but high values also emphasize compression blocks and sharpening halos.
tiktok.step_5_body: Keep the tab visible while the browser records the adjusted video in real time. Play the export once to check the picture and audio before sharing it.
tiktok.compression_title: Why a saved TikTok copy may need gentler settings
tiktok.compression_body_1: Platform processing can rescale the frame and introduce block edges, ringing around text and texture loss. Those changes are different from the filter itself, so stronger denoising or sharpening does not necessarily produce a cleaner result.
tiktok.compression_body_2: A good stopping point is the lightest correction that restores believable skin and neutral objects without making captions crunchy or movement shimmer. Compare the full frame, not only one face or one paused detail.
tiktok.limits_title: What this workflow can and cannot recover
tiktok.limits_body: It can reduce a green cast, added grain and flattened contrast when the original scene remains visible. It cannot reconstruct pixels removed by heavy compression, reveal an unfiltered source that you do not possess or restore content that an effect replaced.
tiktok.faq_q1: Can I paste a TikTok link into this tool?
tiktok.faq_a1: No. The tool accepts a video file from your device and does not fetch or download TikTok URLs. Use a file you own or have permission to edit.
tiktok.faq_q2: Does the video upload to your server?
tiktok.faq_a2: No. Decoding, preview and export happen inside the current browser tab. The site does not receive your media file.
tiktok.faq_q3: Why does my TikTok video look soft after correction?
tiktok.faq_a3: The copy may already contain platform compression, or Noise may be too high. Lower Noise, keep Detail moderate and use the original camera or editor export when possible.
tiktok.faq_q4: Will the exported video keep its sound?
tiktok.faq_a4: The tool attaches audio when the browser can read and verify the source track. It blocks export when sound cannot be verified instead of silently producing a muted result.
tiktok.faq_q5: Can this recreate the exact video from before the filter?
tiktok.faq_a5: No. It corrects visible color, noise and edge contrast in the file you provide. Missing source pixels and details replaced by an effect cannot be recovered exactly.
capcut.meta_title: How to Remove Matcha Filter in CapCut – Source-First Guide
capcut.meta_description: Remove or reduce the Matcha Filter in an editable CapCut project, or correct a baked export with the free local video tool. Follow the right source-first path.
capcut.h1: How to Remove the Matcha Filter in CapCut
capcut.lede: The right fix depends on what you still have: an editable CapCut project or only an exported video. Start there before applying another correction layer.
capcut.decision_title: First, identify which source you have
capcut.decision_project_title: You still have the editable project
capcut.decision_project_body: Open the project and look for the filter, effect or adjustment that creates the Matcha look. Reducing or removing that layer preserves more of the original signal than correcting a finished export.
capcut.decision_export_title: You only have an exported video
capcut.decision_export_body: The look is baked into the pixels. CapCut can apply a second correction, but the local video tool gives you a focused Colour, Noise and Detail workflow without requiring an account or upload.
capcut.project_title: If the CapCut project is still editable
capcut.project_body_1: CapCut's current documentation describes filters with adjustable intensity and effects that can sit as separate timeline tracks. The exact labels and placement can differ between mobile, desktop and web versions, so use the project structure rather than memorizing one button path.
capcut.project_body_2: Duplicate the project before changing it. That gives you a reversible reference and makes it easier to compare the unedited grade with a lighter version.
capcut.step_1_title: Select the filter or effect layer
capcut.step_1_body: Check the selected clip and any separate effect track for the layer responsible for the green grade, grain or texture treatment.
capcut.step_2_body: Reduce the filter intensity gradually and compare skin, whites and shadows. If the look is a separate effect and you do not need it, remove that effect from the timeline.
capcut.step_3_title: Review the whole timeline and export once
capcut.step_3_body: Check cuts, overlays and captions so the change stays consistent between clips. Export from the editable project rather than correcting and re-exporting the same compressed file repeatedly.
capcut.export_title: If the filter is already baked into an export
capcut.export_body_1: A finished video no longer contains a removable filter layer. Use the highest-quality export you have and make one moderate correction pass: Colour first, Noise second and Detail last.
capcut.export_body_2: Avoid stacking aggressive filters. Each extra render can magnify banding, block edges and halos, while no adjustment can recover pixels removed from the earlier export.
capcut.export_cta: Open the local video correction tool
capcut.limits_callout_title: Correction stops at the pixels that survived
capcut.limits_body: Removing an editable layer can return the project closer to its underlying clips. Correcting an export can only improve the pixels that remain; it cannot restore an absent original grade, hidden detail or content replaced by a visual effect.
capcut.sources_intro: CapCut changes its interface across platforms and releases. These official pages explain the current filter-intensity and effect-track concepts; follow the labels shown in your installed version.
capcut.source_effects: CapCut Help: effects and separate timeline tracks
capcut.source_remove: CapCut Help: selecting and deleting an effect or filter asset
capcut.faq_q1: Should I remove the filter in CapCut or use this tool?
capcut.faq_a1: Use CapCut first when the original project is editable because you can reduce or remove the actual layer. Use the local tool when you only have an exported file or need a focused correction pass.
capcut.faq_q2: Why can I not find the same button shown in another tutorial?
capcut.faq_a2: CapCut's mobile, desktop and web interfaces can differ and change over time. Look for the selected clip's filter controls or a separate effect track instead of relying on one fixed menu path.
capcut.faq_q3: Can lowering filter intensity restore the original clip?
capcut.faq_a3: It can move an editable project closer to the source clips. If other adjustments or effects also changed the picture, review those layers too. An exported file does not retain this edit history.
capcut.faq_q4: Will another export reduce video quality?
capcut.faq_a4: It can. Re-encoding may add compression, especially at a lower resolution or bitrate. Start from the best source and avoid repeated correction-and-export cycles.
capcut.faq_q5: Does this site connect to my CapCut account?
capcut.faq_a5: No. The local video workflow accepts a file from your device and runs in the browser. It does not access your CapCut projects or account.
